children: The biggest threat to sterling is likely to come from October's U.K. budget, Societe Generale's Kit Juckes says in a note. Sterling has held up better against the euro than short-term interest rate differentials would suggest, reacting to improved U.K. growth forecasts for 2026. However, potential fiscal austerity could cast doubts over the U.K. economic outlook, he says. A narrowing U.K.-eurozone rate differential and concerns about tighter fiscal policy suggest sterling could weaken this autumn, he says. The euro rises 0.1% to 0.8560 pounds and SocGen sees the risk of it reaching 0.88 in the fourth quarter. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
